statements.passage_as_proposed: Heat generated and exerted from fires can reduce the surrounding humidity levels while also raising the surrounding temperature... The surrounding atmosphere's refractive index is influenced by this phenomenon, resulting in the occurrence of sub-refraction... Atmospheric smoke has been shown [18] to increase radiofrequency (RF) signal attenuation... The presence of particulate matter causes scattering of the radio waves, leading to signal attenuation.

proposal.statement: Fire‑generated heat and combustion products can cause radio‑frequency signal attenuation, primarily through reduced air density, altered refractive index, and scattering by particulate matter.
